reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BitClub Network as a bitcoin investment and mining opportunity, directs viewers to join through a sponsor link and pay fees or buy a mining pool, and claims they can earn money through pool investment and recruitment commissions. It also presents a millionaire-producing vision and a binary team reward of $200 in bitcoins. The legitimacy claim is part of the promotional pitch, but the records do not verify the external URL, compensation terms, participant outcomes, or whether any payments occurred.

citations.quote: So the vision here is to produce 10,000 millionaires. So the vision is big and if you want to be a part of it, Big Club Network is inviting you to join.
So how do you join BigClubNetwork? You pay a one soft fee of $99 and then you buy a mining pool. There are four different mining pools that you could buy.
you could join a Bitcoin mining company such as BitClub Network. What BitClub Network does is that it will incur all the cost for you. It will buy and set up the computers and maintain them for you
There are two ways to make money in BitClub. The first one is when you just buy the pool, you invest, you buy the pool, you do some settings and you leave it to run.
The second way is through network marketing you recruit others and then bitcoin network will pay you for that

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present mining as effortless or cost-free. She says doing it yourself requires equipment and electricity and “could be costly”; she also describes a proposed link between scarcity, demand and price as something “believed,” not certain. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether this is an explanation of mining choices rather than a promise of returns. The claim that a company would handle equipment and electricity describes the alternative she is discussing; it does not, by itself, establish what any purchaser would earn.

citations.quote: You can either do it yourself which requires electricity and the right computers and this could be costly
that is what will cause it to be scarce and increase the demand which is believed to then affect price
It will buy and set up the computers and maintain them for you and even handling the electricity

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fees and invitation to join establish a commercial pitch, but they do not turn the speaker's discussion of mining costs into a guaranteed earnings claim. Likewise, “leave it to run” says little about the amount, timing or certainty of any return. The prosecution's concern about unverified terms is fair, but lack of verification alone does not show that every explanatory claim is deceptive.

citations.quote: You pay a one soft fee of $99 and then you buy a mining pool.
you buy the pool, you do some settings and you leave it to run.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cost qualification concerns mining independently, immediately before the speaker proposes joining the company that would handle those costs. It is not a warning about the risk of buying its pools. The speaker explicitly describes buying a pool as an investment and one way to make money, so uncertainty about the exact return does not erase the solicitation.

citations.quote: You can either do it yourself which requires electricity and the right computers and this could be costly or you could join a Bitcoin mining company such as BitClub Network.
There are two ways to make money in BitClub. The first one is when you just buy the pool, you invest, you buy the pool, you do some settings and you leave it to run.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the presentation's teaching sequence. The speaker proposes to define Bitcoin, cover other cryptocurrencies, explain acquisition and mining, and then discuss the company. She explains that miners verify transactions and that records are stored on a public blockchain. She also lays out buying and holding, trading, and mining as different ways to acquire bitcoin. In that context, the company can be read as an example in an operational lesson. The presence of a joining section does not require treating the whole presentation as a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: First we will start with defining what Bitcoin is We'll look at other types of cryptocurrencies We'll look at how to acquire Bitcoin Mining & blockchain BitClub network How To Join How To Make Money.

miners use specially designed computers and advanced software to verify transactions and then they are rewarded bitcoins and commission so the transactions are kept transparent and are stored on a blockchain for public access.
there are three ways of acquiring bitcoins the first way is to buy and hold just like gold and silver the second way is to buy and sell just like trading and the third way is mining

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution isolates the joining and earnings portions, but the speaker first sets out a broader curriculum on Bitcoin and mining. An explanation can include what joining costs and how a compensation structure purports to work. Those details establish what is being described; without verified transactions or outcomes, they do not establish that the account of the service is false.

citations.quote: We'll look at how to acquire Bitcoin Mining & blockchain BitClub network How To Join How To Make Money.
So how do you join BigClubNetwork? You pay a one soft fee of $99 and then you buy a mining pool.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The introductory lessons do not change where the presentation leads. The speaker invites viewers to join a venture whose stated vision is producing millionaires, then says buying a pool is an investment that can make money. She also offers recruitment as a second earning route. Those are affirmative pitches, not merely neutral descriptions of mining technology.

The second way is through network marketing you recruit others and then bitcoin network will pay you for that

opening.argument: Judge, the described purchase has an identifiable service: the company would buy, set up and maintain mining computers and handle electricity. The speaker distinguishes purchasing a mining pool from a separate referral route, then explains commissions for bringing in buyers. A paid service with a referral program is not, on those facts alone, proof that the service is fictitious or that every buyer must recruit to participate. The record gives proposed prices and compensation terms, but does not establish whether equipment was operated, whether purchasers received returns, or whether the terms were honored. That evidentiary gap should not be filled by assuming an outcome.

citations.quote: It will buy and set up the computers and maintain them for you and even handling the electricity
There are two ways to make money in BitClub. The first one is when you just buy the pool, you invest, you buy the pool, you do some settings and you leave it to run.
The second way is through network marketing you recruit others and then bitcoin network will pay you for that
The first two mining pools you bring in, Big Club Network will pay you a commission of 5%.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker requests a pool purchase and describes recruitment pay. But its own account says the external terms and outcomes are unverified. A purchase requirement and a referral commission do not establish that mining never occurred or that recruitment was required to earn from a purchased pool; the speaker presents pool investment and network marketing as two distinct routes.

citations.quote: There are two ways to make money in BitClub. The first one is when you just buy the pool, you invest, you buy the pool, you do some settings and you leave it to run.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: No finding that equipment was fictitious is needed to recognize what this video promotes. It directs viewers to pay a fee and buy a mining pool, presents that purchase as an investment that can make money, and adds escalating commissions for bringing in more pool buyers. The asserted mining service does not make those paid-return and recruitment claims incidental.
